topics.title: Nature of Thinking and Building Blocks of Thought
topics.ncert_sections: Nature of Thinking; Building Blocks of Thought; Box 7.1

concepts.learning_objective: Describe thinking as a higher mental process that manipulates information and is inferred from behaviour.
Distinguish mental images and concepts as the building blocks of thought and explain why concepts are formed.
Explain how culture shapes analytical and holistic styles of thinking.

topics.title: Problem Solving and Its Obstacles
topics.ncert_sections: Problem Solving; Obstacles to Solving Problems

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the sequence of mental operations involved in solving a problem.
Explain how mental set and functional fixedness hinder problem solving.
Recognise lack of motivation and persistence as an obstacle to problem solving.
Distinguish deductive reasoning (general to particular) from inductive reasoning (particular to general).
Explain analogy as a four-part form of reasoning.
Explain how judgment and decision-making are interrelated yet different processes.
State the criteria of creative thinking: novelty, originality, effective surprise and appropriateness.
Distinguish convergent from divergent thinking and identify fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration.
Explain de Bono's lateral thinking and the six thinking hats technique.

topics.title: Process and Strategies of Creative Thinking
topics.ncert_sections: Process of Creative Thinking; Strategies for Creative Thinking

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the stages of preparation, incubation, illumination and verification.
Explain the principle of brainstorming and other strategies that enhance creative thinking.
Explain Whorf's linguistic relativity hypothesis and its strong version.
Compare Piaget's and Vygotsky's views on the relationship between thought and language.

topics.title: Development of Language and Language Use
topics.ncert_sections: Development of Language and Language Use; Box 7.3

concepts.learning_objective: Identify symbols, rules and communication as the basic characteristics of language.
Sequence the stages of language development from crying to telegraphic speech.
Compare Skinner's learning view and Chomsky's innate view of language acquisition, and explain pragmatic language use.
